body.statement: For \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\), determine the finite Pareto set \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\) over \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}\): integer matrices have \(J\leq J_{\max}\) and entries at most \(m_{\max}\); grids are subsets of the fixed finite rational set \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{cand}}\) with cardinality at most \(L_{\max}\); normalized nonnegative rational allocations and well caps lie in \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{adm}}\subset\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) and \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{adm}}\); and truncation, moment, Taylor, objective-subdivision, chart-subdivision, precision, and arithmetic work obey the fixed policy and \(\mathfrak b\). Can certified dominance and infeasibility rules characterize the finite frontier in graph gap, Jacobian margin, global-identification margins, required wells, contrast half-width, and arithmetic cost without evaluating every admissible input?
body.justification: The question poses a finite auditable design frontier under declared statistical and computational budgets.
body.gap: Validated global optimization certifies numerical ranges, and tomography design optimizes information, but no result characterizes a joint certified region for Poisson-PGF graph exclusion, immersion, and causal-contrast precision.
body.consumer: It yields a reusable finite menu of nondominated prospective designs.
